name: Philippi
overview: Philippi, identified as the chief city of Macedonia and a Roman colony, serves as a significant setting where Paul and his companions ministered and built the early church (Acts 16:12). On the Sabbath, Paul engaged in prayer and teaching by a riverside, leading to the conversion and baptism of Lydia, a God-fearing woman whose heart the Lord opened to receive the gospel (Acts 16:13-15). This passage also highlights the spiritual opposition encountered, as a possessed woman followed Paul, proclaiming him a servant of the Most High God who reveals the way of salvation (Acts 16:16-17). These events underscore Philippi's role as a foundational community in Paul's missionary work and the spread of the gospel.
